verses.1: And these nations were chosen by Jehovah to test Israel with all the things they didn’t know about all their battles in Canaan.
verses.2: Only so that the wisdom of the children of Israel might be taught about warfare, something they did not know before.
verses.3: Five of the Philistines’ kings, along with all the Canaanites, Sidonians, and Hivvites, ruled from Mount Lebanon. They ruled from Mount Baal-Hermon until the time when Hamath came into existence.
verses.4: And they became a test for Israel, to see whether they would obey the commands of Jehovah, which He had given to their ancestors through Moses.
verses.5: And the children of Israel shall dwell among the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivvites, and the Yebusites.
verses.6: And they took their daughters as wives, and they gave their daughters to their sons. And they served their gods.
verses.7: And the children of Israel did evil in the eyes of Jehovah. They forgot Jehovah their God and worshiped their gods and false gods.
verses.8: And Jehovah struck Israel, and they were sold into slavery by Kushan, the king of Aram Naharaim. And the children of Israel obeyed those evil rulers for two years.
verses.9: And the children of Israel cried out to Jehovah. Then Jehovah raised a savior for the children of Israel. And He saved them from Amnon, son of King Kenaan’s brother, the little boy.
verses.10: And there was a breath of Jehovah upon him. He then punished Israel. He went out to fight in battle. And Jehovah placed Kushan, the king of Aram, in his hands. His hand became strong against Kushan, the king of Aram.
verses.11: And the land was quiet for forty years. Then Atniyael, son of Kenaz, died.
verses.12: And the children of Israel committed evil deeds in the eyes of Jehovah. Therefore, Jehovah strengthened Og, king of Moab, against Israel, because they had done evil in the eyes of Jehovah.
verses.13: And he gathered together the sons of Ammon and Amalek against him. He went and attacked Israel, and he took over the city of Timnah.
verses.14: And the children of Israel obeyed Eglon, king Moab’s name was Eleazar. He ruled for twelve years.
verses.15: And the children of Israel cried out to Jehovah. Then Jehovah raised up a savior for them: Ehid, son of Gerah, son of His Right Hand. And the children of Israel sent him as a gift to Jehu, king of Moab.
verses.16: And Ehuad made a chair for him. He also made two legs for it, each of which was long in length. He secured the chair under his right arm.
verses.17: And he brought the offering to Eglon, King Moab, and also to Eglon, a man who was healthy.
verses.18: And when they had finished offering the sacrifices, he sent out the people who were carrying the offerings.
verses.19: And he came back from the depths of darkness. He said, “This is a secret message for you, king.” Then all those who stood on top of him stepped down.
verses.20: And Ehuad came to him. He sat on the high chair that belonged only to him. Ehuad said, “God has spoken to me.” Then he stood up from the throne.
verses.21: And Ehud sent out Shemuel’s hand, and he took the spear from above his right ear, and he stuck it into his own body.
verses.22: And the lamb also came after the fire. It sealed the milk away from the fire, because the lamb hadn’t been slaughtered from its body. Then the priest went out.
verses.23: And Ehuad the organizer went out and closed the doors of the upper rooms behind him, then he left.
verses.24: And he went out, and his servants came forward. They saw that the doors of the upper room were closed. They said, “But how can he enter through those closed doors?”
verses.25: And they opened its doors. But behold, it did not open its doors at all. They took the key and opened it. And behold, its doors fell down to the ground, and it died.
verses.26: And Ehuad was carried away until they were exhausted. Then he passed through the passages, and the stairs were also carried along with him.
verses.27: And when he came out, he stood in the valley of Efraim. The sons of Israel descended from the mountain with him, and he stood before them.
verses.28: And he said to them, “Follow me. For the LORD has given your enemies into your hands.” So they followed him. They captured the people who were crossing the Jordan to go into Egypt. But they didn’t let anyone cross over.
verses.29: And at that time, they killed Moab. It was like twelve thousand men were killed, every one of them a warrior. No one survived.
verses.30: And Moab submitted to Israel that day. The land became peaceful during those years.
verses.31: And after him was Shemgar, the son of Anath. He led out the Philistines during the day. He also saved Israel.
